summary: Jacob cuts a fresh rod from this tree. Hosea describes people choosing its shade, along with that of the oak and terebinth, for their sacrifices.

senses.definition: A shade tree from which rods could be cut. Ancient translators identify it variously as the white poplar and the storax tree.

evidence.note: The first of Jacob’s three kinds of rod is libneh. Peeling the rods exposes the light wood beneath the bark.
The shade is the reason given for burning incense beneath these trees.

evidence.locator: L00100, Onkelos Gen 30:37 and Targum Hos 4:13
s.v. ልብን, naming the tree from which resin is obtained
Book I p. 2046, n29119, ʿasal al-lubnā, and p. 3007, n43218
s.v. lbnt, KTU 1.13:13, discussion of competing readings

note: The Septuagint uses στυρακίνην, ‘of storax’, in Gen.30.37 and λεύκης, ‘of white poplar’, in Hos.4.13. Both renderings are aligned to this Hebrew noun in MACULA-LXX. The Ugaritic word occurs in a simile and its meaning is disputed.
